description: Results from all training experiments. Each run documents parameters, observations, and outcomes to explain how different choices caused different behaviours.

runs.label: Baseline — Pretrained VIPTokens, No Adversarial Training

parameters.training: none — original Stage3 clean training only

key_observations: Pretrained VIPTokens work perfectly on clean images and deepfakes
Completely vulnerable to adversarial attacks — FGSM/PGD drop TransFace sim to 19–63/100 and model says No
Model relies heavily on the similarity score text signal; no mechanism to override it

runs.label: Fine-tune (Pretrained Init) — Wrong Prompt Format, LR=0.001

parameters.training_prompt: short format: 'just say yes or no without explanation'
parameters.eval_prompt: long format: 'explain reasoning step by step based on facial attributes'

key_observations: CRITICAL BUG: Training used short prompt format, evaluation used long prompt — complete distribution mismatch
Near-zero training loss (~0.04) because the short format is trivially answered; model never struggled
Token norm change: 0.019 TOTAL over 3 full epochs — tokens essentially did not move
Zero gradient signal on adversarial examples because model already answered correctly with trivial format
Prompt mismatch meant every gradient step was wasted
LR=0.001 also too low — even if prompt was correct, gradient would be too small
runs.result_file: none — results directory cleared before saving

runs.label: Fine-tune (Pretrained Init) — Correct Prompt, LR=1.0, adv_sim in prompts
key_observations: Prompt fix worked: token norm change jumped to 0.23/step (vs 0.019 total before)
Adversarial loss: ~1.38 initially — model struggling with low-sim + [Yes] label
BUT: LR=1.0 on pretrained tokens caused catastrophic forgetting — normal_real dropped from 100% to 90%
adv_sim in prompt created severe text/label conflict: text says '21/100', label says [Yes]
Model could not reconcile low sim text with authentication label
Gradient conflict: clean examples pushed tokens one way, adversarial pushed another
id0 showed 0% FGSM/PGD even after training — pretrained token fine-tuning proven insufficient
runs.result_file: none — results directory cleared before saving

runs.label: From-Scratch Training — Random Init, orig_sim in prompts, LR=1.0
key_observations: Hypothesis: using original (pre-attack) sim avoids text/label conflict — text says '91/100', label says [Yes]
Training loss healthy: 0.62–0.68, token norm change 2.75/step in epoch 1
Tokens learned from scratch successfully — no catastrophic forgetting since nothing to forget
CRITICAL MISMATCH: training used orig_sim (91/100) but evaluation used adv_sim (47–75/100)
Model learned: 'high sim + VIP tokens → Yes'. At eval: sees 47–75/100, always says No
Root cause: train/eval distribution mismatch on the sim score text signal
Normal_real and deepfake worked because they still see high/medium sim at eval time
id0 normal_real: 86.7% (3 errors at sim=79,82,82 — below learned threshold)
runs.result_file: none — results directory cleared before R4 rerun

runs.label: From-Scratch Training — Random Init, adv_sim in prompts, LR=1.0
key_observations: Fix from R3: switched to adv_sim in training prompts to match eval distribution
Training loss: 0.68, token norm change 0.18/step (lower than R3 — harder learning problem)
Adversarial robustness fully solved: 100% FGSM and PGD across all IDs
CRITICAL FAILURE: deepfake detection collapsed — 0–26% accuracy
Root cause: sim ranges OVERLAP — deepfake sim (52–78/100) and adversarial real sim (47–75/100) are nearly identical
Model learned 'sim 47–75 → Yes' and applied this to deepfakes too
adv_loss dropped to ~0.002 by epoch 3 — adversarial examples fully memorized
With 20% adversarial data all labeled [Yes] and deepfakes also at similar sim, model collapsed toward Yes
Catastrophic tradeoff: fixing FGSM/PGD robustness broke deepfake detection
runs.key_insight: Sim score ranges for adversarial real (47–75) and deepfakes (52–78) overlap by ~20 points. The model cannot distinguish them by text signal alone — VIP tokens must learn visual discrimination. Simultaneous training on both objectives with same sim range proved too ambiguous.

runs.label: Curriculum Training — Stage1 Clean (LR=1.0, ep=3) + Stage2 Adv (LR=0.1, ep=3, adv=15%)

stage1.goal: establish strong deepfake detection and VIP identity learning from scratch

stage2.goal: add adversarial robustness without destroying stage1 deepfake knowledge

runs.hypothesis: By learning deepfake discrimination first (stage 1), VIP tokens develop visual discrimination capability. Stage 2 fine-tunes with adversarial examples at lower LR (10x), adding robustness without erasing visual discrimination.
key_observations: PGD robustness: FULLY SOLVED — 100% across all three IDs despite sim scores of only 14–34/100
Normal real: 100% across all IDs — no regression from baseline
FGSM result is identity-dependent: id2=100%, id0=46.7%, id1=13.3%
Deepfake detection: id0=96.7% (excellent), id1=80% (good), id2=43.3% (poor)
The FGSM/deepfake tradeoff persists at the identity level: id2 solved FGSM but lost deepfake; id0 kept deepfake but partially lost FGSM

Root cause: id2 deepfakes have sim range 54–86 (mean 71.4), heavily overlapping with FGSM range (46–72). With 15% adv_fraction, Stage2 pushed the id2 token toward 'accept medium sim' — fixing FGSM but accepting id2 deepfakes at sim 80–86
id0 deepfakes have sim range 52–78 (mean 62.5), lower overlap with normal_real — curriculum preserved deepfake detection better for id0
The fundamental challenge is not solved for all identities simultaneously: identities whose deepfake sim scores are highest (id2: mean 71.4) suffer most from adversarial training

comparison_vs_baseline.deepfake: ~92% avg → 73% avg (-19pp) — some regression, worst on id2

sim_range_overlap_analysis.description: The fundamental challenge in this problem
sim_range_overlap_analysis.key_overlap: Deepfake and FGSM adversarial real images have nearly identical sim ranges (52–78 vs 47–75). The model cannot use the sim score text signal to distinguish them — only VIP token visual discrimination can.
sim_range_overlap_analysis.implication: Any training strategy that teaches the model to accept low-sim images (for adversarial robustness) risks also teaching it to accept deepfakes. The solution must explicitly teach visual discrimination at this overlapping sim range.
